name: std::indirectly_copyable_storable

declarations.code:
template <class In, class Out>

concept indirectly_copyable_storable =

    std::indirectly_copyable<In, Out> &&

    std::indirectly_writable<Out, std::iter_value_t<In> &> &&

    std::indirectly_writable<Out, const std::iter_value_t<In> &> &&

    std::indirectly_writable<Out, std::iter_value_t<In> &&> &&

    std::indirectly_writable<Out, const std::iter_value_t<In> &&> &&

    std::copyable<std::iter_value_t<In>> &&

    std::constructible_from<std::iter_value_t<In>, std::iter_reference_t<In>> &&

    std::assignable_from<std::iter_value_t<In> &, std::iter_reference_t<In>>;

intro: The indirectly_copyable_storable concept specifies the relationship between an indirectly_readable type and an indirectly_writable type. In addition to indirectly_copyable, this concept specifies that the copy from the indirectly_readable type can be performed via an intermediate object.

sections.title: Semantic requirements
sections.text:
In and Out model std::indirectly_copyable_storable<In, Out> only if given a dereferenceable value i of type In:

After the definition std::iter_value_t<In> obj(*i);, obj is equal to the value previously denoted by *i, and
 if std::iter_reference_t<In> is an rvalue reference type, *i is placed in a valid but unspecified state after the initialization of obj.

sections.title: Equality preservation
sections.text: Expressions declared in requires expressions of the standard library concepts are required to be equality-preserving (except where stated otherwise).

examples.title: Practical example
examples.input: An int pointer iterates over {3, 7} and satisfies indirectly_copyable_storable.
